title: "Comparison of estimation methods for BPOT"
output:
  html_document:
    df_print: paged
---

```{r,echo=FALSE,include=FALSE}
source('../scripts/preprocessing.R')
Dat <- se_ttc
x0 <- 0
source("../scripts/global_vars.R")
```

Here we compare the different estimation methods for the same data

# estim model
```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
# using joint censored likelihood
estim_r1 <- run_single_bpot(Dat, model = "ct", thres = c(u, v),xcrash = x0)
estim_r1$M$estimate
# using joint Poisson likelihood
estim_r2 <- run_single_bpot(Dat, model = "ct", thres = c(u, v),xcrash = x0,likelihood = "poisson")
estim_r2$M$estimate
# using marginal censired likelihood
estim_r3 <- run_single_bpot(Dat, model = "ct", thres = c(u, v),
                          xcrash = x0,estim = "margins")
estim_r3$M$estimate

#  poisson likelihood with marginal approach
estim_r4 <- run_single_bpot(Dat, model = "ct", thres = c(u, v),
                          xcrash = x0,estim = "margins",likelihood = "poisson")
estim_r4$M$estimate


estim_result <- list(censored = estim_r1, poisson = estim_r2)
summarise_bpot(estim_result, severity = pis0, severity_age = pis1)

plot_crash_severity(lapply(estim_result, function(x) x$plot_df), injury_df = injury_df)
```


Conclusion
 - The combination of Bayesian and MLE for estimating non-stationary margin and dependence parameter can be used. However the data does not allow us to see whetehr there is a difference between marginal and joint approach when the margins are mixed with light and heavy tails.
 - the poisson likelihood is similar to the copula likelihood
